sections.body: Taurus, "the bull", is a constellation in the Zodiac so it's close to the ecliptic – the intersection of the celestial sphere with the plane defined by the orbit of the Earth around the Sun. Hence, from our point of view here on Earth, we can regularly find the planets, and also the Sun, in this constellation – in the case of the Sun from May 14 to June 21. (Of course if the Sun is there, we cannot see the constellation's stars.) Taurus is one of the 88 modern constellations defined by the International Astronomical Union, and also one of the 48 classical constellations named by 2nd century astronomer Claudius Ptolemy. In the northern hemisphere, it's prominently visible in the night sky in winter. Its brightest star is the reddish Aldebaran.

Winter Constellations

Caption: Second place in the 2022 IAU OAE Astrophotography Contest, category Time lapses of celestial patterns.   Sirius, the brightest star in the night sky, is shown rising, setting and passing by. Sometimes constellations and asterisms are also visible, including Orion, Taurus and the Pleiades. In the first scene, the aforementioned constellations are covered by a semi-transparent golden veil. The next scenes show it rising in a dark blue night sky. In one of the scenes, a planet brightly decorates the faint constellation Pisces. The videos were taken above various landscapes and places of cultural heritage on Earth. Some of them simply show monuments in the desert, while others show palm trees with waving leaves.
Credit: Amirreza Kamkar/IAU OAE

License: CC-BY-4.0 Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0) icons


Warm Winter Night Over Spiš Region

Caption: Winner in the 2022 IAU OAE Astrophotography Contest, category Still images of celestial patterns.   This image, taken in Slovakia in January 2022, shows regions of the Milky Way and a rich variety of constellations. The summer constellations of the northern hemisphere are very low in the sky towards the bottom-right. The bright stars of Cygnus and Lyra shine through the artificial lights at the horizon. The huge array of northern winter and autumn constellations with many bright stars are associated with diverse cultural stories. For the Lakota people in North America the belt of the Orion constellation represents the spine of a bison (“Tayamnicankh”). Orion, the Hunter of Greek mythology, is sometimes described chasing the Seven Sisters, the Pleiades. The Arabs transformed this view by considering the follower of the Pleiades only one star instead of a constellation. Aldebaran, the star in the right eye of Taurus, the Bull, comes from this interpretation, because the name Aldebaran derives from al-dabaran, The Follower. At the bottom-right, on the horizon, we can see the milky lightcone of the Zodiacal light stretching from the constellation Pisces through Aries, almost reaching the Pleiades, indicating the path of the planets and the Moon in this area. The Pleiades and the Hyades together form a gate on this path, where the heavenly bodies occasionally pass before entering the Milky Way. The planets were considered sheep in ancient Babylon and the modern constellation Orion was considered the “True Shepherd” of the Sky, with his shepherd’s tool reaching the ecliptic. In Roman tradition, the bright white star above the Pleiades and the Milky Way is called Capella, the Goat, which can be traced back to an Egyptian constellation in this area. Above the treetop in the middle-right part of the image, we see the autumn square, the Andromeda Galaxy and the W-shaped pattern of Cassiopeia. To the left of this group, in the central part of the visible Milky Way, is the constellation Perseus, with Cepheus in the dark area above Cassiopeia completing the celestial family. The Andromeda saga is a Greek story from the area that is now called Israel, and is rooted in Syrian traditions. The location of Andromeda was considered by the ancient Babylonians as the location of the goddess of sexual love, and by the Syrians as the location of the goddess of fertility. According to the saga, Andromeda was chained to a rock at the coast of Jaffa (Tel Aviv) in order to protect her land from a sea monster. The name of the hero who rescued her is Perseus, probably meaning “from Persia” (today’s Iran). Noticeable in the valley are the lights from towns. The yellow light above the horizon indicates larger cities there, which are given away by their light pollution.
Credit: Robert Barsa/IAU OAE

Romanian Orion

Caption: Winner in the 2022 IAU OAE Astrophotography Contest, category Still images of celestial patterns.   Taken in Romania in August 2012, this image shows two of the most recognisable constellations in the sky, Orion and Taurus. Orion, the Hunter, is found near the horizon. The most prominent star visible in this image is Betelgeuse, while the asterism of Orion’s belt is formed by three aligned bright stars. Just above Orion we can find Taurus, one of the constellations of the Zodiac. As the Zodiac is inherited from Babylon, The Bull of Heaven represents a mighty but dangerous creature that was defeated by King Gilgamesh and his friend Enkidu. They cut the Bull in half and sacrificed the animal to the gods in order to protect their people. Taurus is also home to the star cluster Pleiades, also known as the Seven Sisters. Two planets are visible: Venus, the bright spot near the fence, and Jupiter, the bright spot at the top, next to the Bull’s face. Different cultures have included the stars of these constellations in their own mythology. The Romanians, for instance, after Christianisation identified four other constellations using some of the stars of Orion and others surrounding it. One such constellation is called Trisfetitele (the Three Saints), which is associated with the three stars comprising Orion's Belt, representing the Three Hierarchs Basil, Gregory and John. This same asterism is also called Three Wise Men, Kings from the East or just Three Kings — all of these names being rooted in the Christian religion. The agricultural calendar, in contrast, led farmers to define two other constellations, the Little Plough and the Sickle. Both are seen in the southern half of the Orion rectangle; the Little Plough is drawn by connecting the southern quadrilateral with Orion’s left shoulder, and the Sickle is formed by connecting Orion’s left foot (Rigel) with the belt stars, forming an arch and completing the form of a hoe. In the cultural calendar, these constellations were used to announce the harvest of wheat/grain. Finally, the fourth Romanian constellation is the Great Auger, where Orion’s belt represents the handle of the auger, and Betelgeuse is the tip, facing towards Pollux in Gemini. This constellation is associated with treasure, as Romanian peasants believe that the Auger points to the treasure when they approach the end of the world. Most of the official star names in Orion are Arabic; Mintaka (meaning “belt”) is at the waist; Alnitak (meaning “girdle”) and Alnilam (meaning “string”) are at the belt; and Rigel (meaning foot) is at the left foot. The star on the left shoulder is named Bellatrix, the Latin term for a female warrior. The star at the right leg is called Saiph, for the sword or sabre of the Arabic Orion.
Credit: Alex Conu/IAU OAE

Winter Milky Way

Caption: Winner in the 2022 IAU OAE Astrophotography Contest, category Still images of celestial patterns.   Taken near Lake Misurina in the Veneto region of Italy in February 2019, this image shows a clear and starry sky over a winter landscape. We can see part of the Milky Way arc. From the left side, towards the south-east, we see Sirius, "The Burner" in Greek, the brightest star in the night sky. It is part of the constellation Canis Major, The Great Dog, one of the dogs of Orion, the great hunter, in Greek mythology. Orion’s other dog, Canis Minor, the Small Dog, is represented by the bright star Procyon and its fainter neighbours. The Greek star name means “The One [rising] before The Dog” and the star is seen at the top left side of the image just above the arc of the Galaxy. Orion lies to the right of Canis Major. We can spot its characteristic “belt”, an asterism composed of three bright stars aligned in a straight line.  Above the treetops to the right of Orion, the open star clusters of the Hyades and the Pleiades in the constellation Taurus, the Bull, are visible. According to ancient lore, these two clusters form a Celestial Gate directly next to the intersection of the great circles of the ecliptic and the Milky Way. In Greco-Roman mythology, Taurus is associated with the god Zeus who is said to have used a bull to seduce the Phoenician princess Europa. Above the constellation Taurus, we can see a bright star just above the arc of the Galaxy. This is Capella, the brightest star of the constellation Auriga, The Charioteer. This is one of the 88 modern constellations and is associated with the Greek hero Erichthonius of Athens. Hindu astronomy considers Capella as the heart of Brahma, one of the three major gods. The indigenous people of Bororo in Brazil have a constellation representing a cayman, comprising some of the stars of Auriga and some stars from neighbouring constellations. To the right of Taurus, we find the modern constellation Perseus with the bright double star cluster h+chi Perseii, which represents the metal of Perseus’s sabre in Greek mythology. Perseus is the hero who was sent out to prove himself, and happened to rescue Andromeda from the sea monster Cetus as the Roman poet Ovid wrote. We can also see the constellation Cassiopeia, associated with the queen and mother of Andromeda in Greek mythology. It is composed of five bright stars in the shape of a W, which was considered the asterism of The Key by the Greeks according to the poet Aratus. The recognisable shape is also associated with other mythologies: for instance, it represents the princess Sharmishtha in Hindu astronomy, a bat in Thailand, and a camel in native Arabic astronomy. In the gap between the trees, the Andromeda Galaxy is visible.
Credit: Giorgia Hofer/IAU OAE

Winter Constellations

Caption: Winner in the 2022 IAU OAE Astrophotography Contest, category Still images of celestial patterns. Taken from the Kottamia Astronomical Observatory, Cairo, Egypt, in December 2021, this image shows a few prominent winter constellations of the northern sky above the largest telescope in North Africa. The photograph depicts the constellation of Orion (prominently in the middle of the image) with its belt of stars pointing up to Aldebaran in Taurus and down to Sirius in Canis Major. Aldebaran is a reddish star that we see in front of the open star cluster of the Hyades (at the upper right edge of the image), which is the face of Taurus, the bull. The bright white star is Sirius, the brightest star in the night sky. Its Greek name (Seirios) means “the burner” and can be understood metaphorically as “the brightest”. This constellation has been represented in a variety of different cultures from all over the world. The ancient Egyptian religion also associates the constellation of Orion with a male figure, namely the god Osiris. It is told that Osiris was murdered by his envious brother Seth, who then dismembered the body and scattered the pieces all over the land. Fortunately, Osiris’s sister-wife Aset (Greek: Isis) is the most powerful sorceress and protective mother goddess. She collected the pieces, put them back together and breathed life back into the god. Aset is seen in the star pattern around the bright star Sirius at the bottom of the photograph. The Egyptian name for Sirius (and adjacent areas) is Sopdet (Greek: Sothis). The heliacal rise of Sirius in summer was a harbinger of the Egyptian new year.  Going north, we can spot a bluish star. This is Alhena, one of the stars in the feet of the zodiacal constellation Gemini, the twins, whose bright head stars would be beyond the upper left edge of the photograph. In the top centre we can see the star Elnath, in the constellation of Auriga, the charioteer. It is associated with Erichthonius, a hero of Greek mythology believed to be the inventor of the four-horse chariot. This same star is also considered the tip of the upper horn of Taurus, the bull. In Greek mythology Taurus is associated with the god Zeus who had sent him to rob a princess. It is commonly known that this Greek story was invented in order to include the Babylonian constellation in Greek mythology. In the Mesopotamian Gilgamesh saga, which is one of the oldest pieces of literature that we know (being traced back to the 3rd millennium), Taurus is the bull of heaven, sent by a jealous goddess and defeated by the king of Uruk to save his people. In the sky it harbours several interesting astronomical objects.
Credit: Mohamed Aboushelib/IAU OAE

Orion Constellation Map

Caption: The constellation Orion along with its bright stars and surrounding constellations. Orion is surrounded by (going clockwise from the top) Taurus, Eridanus, Lepus, Monoceros and Gemini. Orion’s brightest stars Betelgeuse and Rigel appear at the northern (upper on this diagram) and southern (lower) end of the constellation respectively with the famous three star “belt” in the middle. Orion spans the celestial equator and is thus visible at some time in the year from all of planet Earth. In the most arctic or antarctic regions of the world, some parts of the constellation may not be visible. Orion is most visible in the evenings in the northern hemisphere winter and southern hemisphere summer. The blue line above Orion marks the ecliptic, the path the Sun appears to travel across the sky over the course of a year. The Sun never passes through Orion, but one can occasionally find the other planets of the Solar System and the Moon in Orion. Just south of Orion’s belt lie two Messier objects M42 (the Orion nebula) and M43, marked by green squares. These nebulae along with M78 (here the green square to the left of the belt) are part of the huge Orion Molecular Cloud Complex. This covers most of the constellation and includes regions where these molecular clouds are collapsing to form young starts. The y-axis of this diagram is in degrees of declination with north as up and the x-axis is in hours of right ascension with east to the left. The sizes of the stars marked here relate to the star's apparent magnitude, a measure of its apparent brightness. The larger dots represent brighter stars. The Greek letters mark the brightest stars in the constellation. These are ranked by brightness with the brightest star being labeled alpha, the second brightest beta, etc., although this ordering is not always followed exactly. The circle around Betelgeuse indicates that it is a variable star. The dotted boundary lines mark the IAU's boundaries of the constellations and the solid green lines mark one of the common forms used to represent the figures of the constellations. Neither the constellation boundaries, nor the line marking the ecliptic, nor the lines joining the stars appear on the sky.

Aries lies just north of the celestial equator and is thus visible at some time in the year from all of planet Earth except for the most antarctic regions of the world. Taurus Constellation Map

Caption: The constellation Taurus along with its bright stars and surrounding constellations. Taurus is surrounded by (going clockwise from the top) Perseus, Aries, Cetus, Eridanus, Orion, Gemini and Auriga. Taurus’s brightest star Aldebaran appears in the middle of the constellation. Taurus lies on the ecliptic (shown here as a blue line), this is the path the Sun appears to take across the sky over the course of a year. The Sun is in Taurus from mid May to late June. The other planets of the Solar System can often be found in Taurus. Taurus lies mostly north of the celestial equator with a small part in the celestial southern hemisphere. The whole constellation is visible at some point in the year to whole planet except for the Antarctic and a small region around the North Pole. Taurus is most visible in the evenings in the northern hemisphere winter and southern hemisphere summer. In the eastern part of Taurus we can find the supernova remnant M1 (commonly known as the Crab Nebula), marked here with a green square. In Taurus’s north-east find one of the sky’s most famous open stars clusters M45 (the Pleiades), marked here with a yellow circle. Many of the stars near Aldebaran (but not) Aldebaran are members of another star cluster, the Hyades. However this cluster is close to the solar system so is too dispersed on the sky to have a Messier object designation like the Pleiades has. Gemini Constellation Map

Caption: The zodiac constellation Gemini and its surrounding constellations. Starting from the top of the diagram and going clockwise, these are Auriga, Taurus, Lynx, Orion, Monoceros, Canis Minor and Cancer. The brightest stars in Gemini, Castor and Pollux appear in the upper lefthand corner (north-east) of the diagram. In Greek mythology, the stars in this constellation are thought to resemble twins with their arms wrapped around each other, with Castor and Pollux indicating their heads. Gemini lies on the ecliptic (shown here as a blue line), this is the path the Sun appears to take across the sky over the course of a year. The Sun is in Gemini from late June to late July. The other planets of the Solar System can often be found in Gemini. Gemini lies north of the celestial equator and is visible in all but the antarctic regions of the world. Gemini is most visible in the evenings in the northern hemisphere winter and southern hemisphere summer. Just to the right of the foot of the Castor twin is an open cluster of stars (labelled as a yellow circle with a dotted line border), Messier 35, also known as the Shoe-Buckle Cluster. This cluster is spread out over an area roughly the size of the full moon. In addition to this cluster of stars, there is a planetary nebula (labelled as a green circle with four radial spikes) – NGC 2392 – near the celestial equator and just to the left of the Pollux twin. Two variable stars (Mekbuda and Propus; labelled as two concentric circles) can be found in the “legs” of each twin, but are so faint that an observer would need dark skies to see them. The y-axis of this diagram is in degrees of declination with north as up and the x-axis is in hours of right ascension with east to the left. The sizes of the stars marked here relate to the star's apparent magnitude, a measure of its apparent brightness. The larger dots represent brighter stars. The Greek letters mark the brightest stars in the constellation. These are ranked by brightness with the brightest star being labelled alpha, the second brightest beta, etc., although this ordering is not always followed exactly. Auriga Constellation Map

Caption: The constellation Auriga with its bright stars and surrounding constellations. Auriga is surrounded by (going clockwise from the top): Camelopardalis, Perseus, Taurus, Gemini and Lynx. Capella, the brightest star in Auriga, is the sixth brightest star in the night sky. As a northern constellation, Auriga is visible from the whole of the northern hemisphere at some point in the year. The whole of the constellation is visible to equatorial regions of the southern hemisphere with parts of it visible to temperate southern regions. The whole constellation is circumpolar from arctic regions. The constellation is best viewed in the evening in the late northern hemisphere winter and late southern hemisphere summer. Auriga lies in the plane of the Milky Way and thus hosts a number of open clusters. Of these M36, M37 and M38 are marked on this diagram with yellow circles. IC 405, also known as the flaming star nebula, is marked here with a green square. The y-axis of this diagram is in degrees of declination with north as up and the x-axis is in hours of right ascension with east to the left. The sizes of the stars marked here relate to the star's apparent magnitude, a measure of its apparent brightness. The larger dots represent brighter stars. Sirius, the brightest star in the night sky, is shown rising, setting and passing by. Sometimes constellations and asterisms are also visible, including Orion, Taurus and the Pleiades. In the first scene, the aforementioned constellations are covered by a semi-transparent golden veil. The next scenes show it rising in a dark blue night sky. The videos were taken above various landscapes and places of cultural heritage on Earth. Some of them simply show monuments in the desert, while others show palm trees with waving leaves.

media.caption_en:
Winner in the 2022 IAU OAE Astrophotography Contest, category Still images of celestial patterns.

 

This image, taken in Slovakia in January 2022, shows regions of the Milky Way and a rich variety of constellations. The summer constellations of the northern hemisphere are very low in the sky towards the bottom-right. The bright stars of Cygnus and Lyra shine through the artificial lights at the horizon. The huge array of northern winter and autumn constellations with many bright stars are associated with diverse cultural stories.

For the Lakota people in North America the belt of the Orion constellation represents the spine of a bison (“Tayamnicankh”). Orion, the Hunter of Greek mythology, is sometimes described chasing the Seven Sisters, the Pleiades. The Arabs transformed this view by considering the follower of the Pleiades only one star instead of a constellation. Aldebaran, the star in the right eye of Taurus, the Bull, comes from this interpretation, because the name Aldebaran derives from al-dabaran, The Follower.

At the bottom-right, on the horizon, we can see the milky lightcone of the Zodiacal light stretching from the constellation Pisces through Aries, almost reaching the Pleiades, indicating the path of the planets and the Moon in this area. The Pleiades and the Hyades together form a gate on this path, where the heavenly bodies occasionally pass before entering the Milky Way. The planets were considered sheep in ancient Babylon and the modern constellation Orion was considered the “True Shepherd” of the Sky, with his shepherd’s tool reaching the ecliptic. In Roman tradition, the bright white star above the Pleiades and the Milky Way is called Capella, the Goat, which can be traced back to an Egyptian constellation in this area.

Above the treetop in the middle-right part of the image, we see the autumn square, the Andromeda Galaxy and the W-shaped pattern of Cassiopeia. To the left of this group, in the central part of the visible Milky Way, is the constellation Perseus, with Cepheus in the dark area above Cassiopeia completing the celestial family. The Andromeda saga is a Greek story from the area that is now called Israel, and is rooted in Syrian traditions. The location of Andromeda was considered by the ancient Babylonians as the location of the goddess of sexual love, and by the Syrians as the location of the goddess of fertility. According to the saga, Andromeda was chained to a rock at the coast of Jaffa (Tel Aviv) in order to protect her land from a sea monster. The name of the hero who rescued her is Perseus, probably meaning “from Persia” (today’s Iran).

Noticeable in the valley are the lights from towns. The yellow light above the horizon indicates larger cities there, which are given away by their light pollution.
media.caption_ru:
Победитель конкурса астрофотографии IAU OAE 2022 в категории «Неподвижные изображения небесных узоров».

 

Этот снимок, сделанный в Словакии в январе 2022 года, показывает области Млечного Пути и богатое разнообразие созвездий. Летние созвездия северного полушария находятся очень низко над горизонтом в правом нижнем углу. Яркие звёзды Лебедя и Лиры сияют сквозь искусственные огни на горизонте. Огромное множество северных зимних и осенних созвездий со многими яркими звёздами связано с разнообразными культурными историями.

Для народа лакота в Северной Америке пояс созвездия Ориона представляет позвоночник бизона («Тайамничанкх»). Орион, Охотник из греческой мифологии, иногда описывается как преследующий Семь Сестёр, Плеяды. Арабы изменили это представление, считая последователя Плеяд только одной звездой вместо созвездия. Альдебаран, звезда в правом глазу Тельца, происходит из этой интерпретации, потому что имя Альдебаран происходит от аль-дабаран, Последователь.

В правом нижнем углу, на горизонте, мы можем видеть молочный световой конус зодиакального света, простирающийся от созвездия Рыб через Овна, почти достигая Плеяд, указывая путь планет и Луны в этой области. Плеяды и Гиады вместе образуют врата на этом пути, где небесные тела иногда проходят перед входом в Млечный Путь. Планеты считались овцами в древнем Вавилоне, а современное созвездие Ориона считалось «Истинным Пастырем» Неба, и его пастуший инструмент достигал эклиптики. В римской традиции яркая белая звезда над Плеядами и Млечным Путём называется Капелла, Коза, что восходит к египетскому созвездию в этой области.

Над верхушкой дерева в средней правой части изображения мы видим осенний квадрат, галактику Андромеды и W-образный узор Кассиопеи. Слева от этой группы, в центральной части видимого Млечного Пути, находится созвездие Персея, а Цефей в тёмной области над Кассиопеей завершает небесную семью. Сага об Андромеде — это греческая история из области, которая сейчас называется Израилем, и уходит корнями в сирийские традиции. Местоположение Андромеды считалось древними вавилонянами местом богини сексуальной любви, а сирийцами — местом богини плодородия. Согласно саге, Андромеда была прикована к скале на побережье Яффы (Тель-Авив), чтобы защитить свою землю от морского чудовища. Имя героя, спасшего её, — Персей, вероятно, означающее «из Персии» (сегодняшний Иран).

В долине заметны огни городов. Жёлтый свет над горизонтом указывает на более крупные города, которые выдают себя своим световым загрязнением.

media.caption_en:
Winner in the 2022 IAU OAE Astrophotography Contest, category Still images of celestial patterns.

 

Taken in Romania in August 2012, this image shows two of the most recognisable constellations in the sky, Orion and Taurus.

Orion, the Hunter, is found near the horizon. The most prominent star visible in this image is Betelgeuse, while the asterism of Orion’s belt is formed by three aligned bright stars. Just above Orion we can find Taurus, one of the constellations of the Zodiac. As the Zodiac is inherited from Babylon, The Bull of Heaven represents a mighty but dangerous creature that was defeated by King Gilgamesh and his friend Enkidu. They cut the Bull in half and sacrificed the animal to the gods in order to protect their people. Taurus is also home to the star cluster Pleiades, also known as the Seven Sisters. Two planets are visible: Venus, the bright spot near the fence, and Jupiter, the bright spot at the top, next to the Bull’s face.

Different cultures have included the stars of these constellations in their own mythology. The Romanians, for instance, after Christianisation identified four other constellations using some of the stars of Orion and others surrounding it. One such constellation is called Trisfetitele (the Three Saints), which is associated with the three stars comprising Orion's Belt, representing the Three Hierarchs Basil, Gregory and John. This same asterism is also called Three Wise Men, Kings from the East or just Three Kings — all of these names being rooted in the Christian religion.

The agricultural calendar, in contrast, led farmers to define two other constellations, the Little Plough and the Sickle. Both are seen in the southern half of the Orion rectangle; the Little Plough is drawn by connecting the southern quadrilateral with Orion’s left shoulder, and the Sickle is formed by connecting Orion’s left foot (Rigel) with the belt stars, forming an arch and completing the form of a hoe. In the cultural calendar, these constellations were used to announce the harvest of wheat/grain. Finally, the fourth Romanian constellation is the Great Auger, where Orion’s belt represents the handle of the auger, and Betelgeuse is the tip, facing towards Pollux in Gemini. This constellation is associated with treasure, as Romanian peasants believe that the Auger points to the treasure when they approach the end of the world.

Most of the official star names in Orion are Arabic; Mintaka (meaning “belt”) is at the waist; Alnitak (meaning “girdle”) and Alnilam (meaning “string”) are at the belt; and Rigel (meaning foot) is at the left foot. The star on the left shoulder is named Bellatrix, the Latin term for a female warrior. The star at the right leg is called Saiph, for the sword or sabre of the Arabic Orion.
media.caption_ru:
Победитель конкурса астрофотографии IAU OAE 2022 года, категория «Неподвижные изображения небесных узоров».

 

Снятое в Румынии в августе 2012 года, это изображение показывает два самых узнаваемых созвездия на небе — Орион и Телец.

Орион, Охотник, находится у горизонта. Самая заметная звезда на этом изображении — Бетельгейзе, а астеризм пояса Ориона образован тремя выстроенными в линию яркими звёздами. Чуть выше Ориона мы можем найти Тельца, одно из созвездий Зодиака. Поскольку Зодиак унаследован от Вавилона, Небесный Бык представляет могущественное, но опасное существо, которое было побеждено царём Гильгамешем и его другом Энкиду. Они разрубили Быка пополам и принесли животное в жертву богам, чтобы защитить свой народ. В Тельце также находится звёздное скопление Плеяды, известное также как Семь Сестёр. Видны две планеты: Венера, яркое пятно возле забора, и Юпитер, яркое пятно вверху, рядом с мордой Быка.

Разные культуры включали звёзды этих созвездий в свою мифологию. Например, румыны после христианизации выделили четыре других созвездия, используя некоторые звёзды Ориона и другие окружающие его. Одно такое созвездие называется Трисфетителе (Три Святителя), которое связано с тремя звёздами, составляющими пояс Ориона, представляющими трёх иерархов Василия, Григория и Иоанна. Этот же астеризм также называют Тремя волхвами, Царями с Востока или просто Тремя царями — все эти названия уходят корнями в христианскую религию.

Сельскохозяйственный календарь, напротив, побудил фермеров определить два других созвездия — Малый Плуг и Серп. Оба видны в южной половине прямоугольника Ориона; Малый Плуг образован соединением южного четырёхугольника с левым плечом Ориона, а Серп образуется соединением левой ступни Ориона (Ригель) со звёздами пояса, образуя дугу и завершая форму мотыги. В культурном календаре эти созвездия использовались для объявления урожая пшеницы/зерна. Наконец, четвёртое румынское созвездие — Великий Бур, где пояс Ориона представляет рукоятку бура, а Бетельгейзе — остриё, направленное к Поллуксу в Близнецах. Это созвездие связано с сокровищами, так как румынские крестьяне верят, что Бур указывает на сокровище, когда они приближаются к концу мира.

Большинство официальных названий звёзд в Орионе — арабские; Минтака (означающая «пояс») находится на талии; Альнитак (означающий «кушак») и Альнилам (означающий «нить») находятся на поясе; а Ригель (означающий «нога») находится на левой ноге. Звезда на левом плече называется Беллатрикс, латинский термин для женщины-воина. Звезда на правой ноге называется Сайф, что означает меч или саблю арабского Ориона.

media.caption_en:
Winner in the 2022 IAU OAE Astrophotography Contest, category Still images of celestial patterns.

 

Taken near Lake Misurina in the Veneto region of Italy in February 2019, this image shows a clear and starry sky over a winter landscape.

We can see part of the Milky Way arc. From the left side, towards the south-east, we see Sirius, "The Burner" in Greek, the brightest star in the night sky. It is part of the constellation Canis Major, The Great Dog, one of the dogs of Orion, the great hunter, in Greek mythology. Orion’s other dog, Canis Minor, the Small Dog, is represented by the bright star Procyon and its fainter neighbours. The Greek star name means “The One [rising] before The Dog” and the star is seen at the top left side of the image just above the arc of the Galaxy. Orion lies to the right of Canis Major. We can spot its characteristic “belt”, an asterism composed of three bright stars aligned in a straight line. 

Above the treetops to the right of Orion, the open star clusters of the Hyades and the Pleiades in the constellation Taurus, the Bull, are visible. According to ancient lore, these two clusters form a Celestial Gate directly next to the intersection of the great circles of the ecliptic and the Milky Way. In Greco-Roman mythology, Taurus is associated with the god Zeus who is said to have used a bull to seduce the Phoenician princess Europa.

Above the constellation Taurus, we can see a bright star just above the arc of the Galaxy. This is Capella, the brightest star of the constellation Auriga, The Charioteer. This is one of the 88 modern constellations and is associated with the Greek hero Erichthonius of Athens. Hindu astronomy considers Capella as the heart of Brahma, one of the three major gods. The indigenous people of Bororo in Brazil have a constellation representing a cayman, comprising some of the stars of Auriga and some stars from neighbouring constellations.

To the right of Taurus, we find the modern constellation Perseus with the bright double star cluster h+chi Perseii, which represents the metal of Perseus’s sabre in Greek mythology. Perseus is the hero who was sent out to prove himself, and happened to rescue Andromeda from the sea monster Cetus as the Roman poet Ovid wrote. We can also see the constellation Cassiopeia, associated with the queen and mother of Andromeda in Greek mythology. It is composed of five bright stars in the shape of a W, which was considered the asterism of The Key by the Greeks according to the poet Aratus. The recognisable shape is also associated with other mythologies: for instance, it represents the princess Sharmishtha in Hindu astronomy, a bat in Thailand, and a camel in native Arabic astronomy.

In the gap between the trees, the Andromeda Galaxy is visible.
media.caption_ru:
Победитель конкурса астрофотографии Управления астрономического образования МАС 2022 года в категории «Фотографии узоров звёздного неба».

На снимке, сделанном в феврале 2019 года возле озера Мизурина в итальянской области Венето, видно ясное звёздное небо над зимним пейзажем.

В кадр вошла часть дуги Млечного Пути. Слева, на юго-востоке, виден Сириус — ярчайшая звезда ночного неба. Её название по-гречески означает «пламенеющий». Сириус находится в созвездии Большого Пса, одной из двух собак охотника Ориона в греческой мифологии. Другую собаку, Малого Пса, обозначают яркий Процион и более тусклые звёзды рядом с ним. Название Процион означает «восходящий раньше Пса». Звезда видна слева вверху над дугой Млечного Пути. Правее Большого Пса находится Орион. Его легко узнать по Поясу — трём ярким звёздам, выстроившимся в линию.

Над верхушками деревьев справа от Ориона видны Гиады и Плеяды — рассеянные звёздные скопления в созвездии Тельца. Согласно древнему преданию, они образуют Небесные Врата рядом с пересечением больших кругов эклиптики и Млечного Пути. В греко-римской мифологии Тельца связывают с Зевсом, который в облике быка завладел вниманием финикийской царевны Европы.

Выше Тельца, над дугой Млечного Пути, видна Капелла — ярчайшая звезда Возничего. Это одно из 88 современных созвездий. Греки связывали его с афинским героем Эрихтонием. В индийской традиции Капеллу считают сердцем Брахмы, одного из трёх главных богов. У народа бороро в Бразилии часть звёзд Возничего и соседних созвездий образует фигуру каймана.

Правее Тельца находится созвездие Персея с ярким двойным скоплением h и χ Персея, которое в греческой мифологии изображает металл меча Персея. Герой отправился в путь, чтобы проявить себя, и спас Андромеду от морского чудовища Кита, о чём писал римский поэт Овидий. На снимке видна и Кассиопея, названная в честь мифической царицы, матери Андромеды. Пять её ярких звёзд образуют букву W. По словам греческого поэта Арата, греки видели в этой фигуре ключ. В других традициях фигура тоже получила свои названия. В Индии она изображает царевну Шармиштху, в Таиланде — летучую мышь, а в арабской традиции — верблюда.

В просвете между деревьями видна галактика Андромеды.

media.caption_en:
Winner in the 2022 IAU OAE Astrophotography Contest, category Still images of celestial patterns.

Taken from the Kottamia Astronomical Observatory, Cairo, Egypt, in December 2021, this image shows a few prominent winter constellations of the northern sky above the largest telescope in North Africa.

The photograph depicts the constellation of Orion (prominently in the middle of the image) with its belt of stars pointing up to Aldebaran in Taurus and down to Sirius in Canis Major. Aldebaran is a reddish star that we see in front of the open star cluster of the Hyades (at the upper right edge of the image), which is the face of Taurus, the bull. The bright white star is Sirius, the brightest star in the night sky. Its Greek name (Seirios) means “the burner” and can be understood metaphorically as “the brightest”.

This constellation has been represented in a variety of different cultures from all over the world. The ancient Egyptian religion also associates the constellation of Orion with a male figure, namely the god Osiris. It is told that Osiris was murdered by his envious brother Seth, who then dismembered the body and scattered the pieces all over the land. Fortunately, Osiris’s sister-wife Aset (Greek: Isis) is the most powerful sorceress and protective mother goddess. She collected the pieces, put them back together and breathed life back into the god. Aset is seen in the star pattern around the bright star Sirius at the bottom of the photograph. The Egyptian name for Sirius (and adjacent areas) is Sopdet (Greek: Sothis). The heliacal rise of Sirius in summer was a harbinger of the Egyptian new year. 

Going north, we can spot a bluish star. This is Alhena, one of the stars in the feet of the zodiacal constellation Gemini, the twins, whose bright head stars would be beyond the upper left edge of the photograph. In the top centre we can see the star Elnath, in the constellation of Auriga, the charioteer. It is associated with Erichthonius, a hero of Greek mythology believed to be the inventor of the four-horse chariot. This same star is also considered the tip of the upper horn of Taurus, the bull. In Greek mythology Taurus is associated with the god Zeus who had sent him to rob a princess. It is commonly known that this Greek story was invented in order to include the Babylonian constellation in Greek mythology. In the Mesopotamian Gilgamesh saga, which is one of the oldest pieces of literature that we know (being traced back to the 3rd millennium), Taurus is the bull of heaven, sent by a jealous goddess and defeated by the king of Uruk to save his people. In the sky it harbours several interesting astronomical objects.
media.caption_ru:
Победитель в 2022 конкурсе астрофотографии IAU OAE, категория «Неподвижные изображения небесных узоров».

Снято в Астрономической обсерватории Коттамия, Каир, Египет, в декабре 2021, это изображение показывает несколько заметных зимних созвездий северного неба над крупнейшим телескопом Северной Африки.

На фотографии изображено созвездие Ориона (заметно в середине изображения) с его поясом звезд, указывающим вверх на Альдебаран в Тельце и вниз на Сириус в Большом Псе. Альдебаран — красноватая звезда, которую мы видим перед рассеянным звездным скоплением Гиады (на верхнем правом краю изображения), которое является лицом Тельца, быка. Яркая белая звезда — Сириус, самая яркая звезда ночного неба. Его греческое название (Seirios) означает «жгучий» и может пониматься метафорически как «самый яркий».

Это созвездие было представлено в различных культурах по всему миру. Древнеегипетская религия также связывает созвездие Ориона с мужской фигурой, а именно с богом Осирисом. Говорят, что Осирис был убит своим завистливым братом Сетом, который затем расчленил тело и разбросал части по всей земле. К счастью, сестра-жена Осириса Асет (греч.: Исида) — самая могущественная волшебница и защитница-богиня-мать. Она собрала части, соединила их и вдохнула жизнь обратно в бога. Асет видна в звездном узоре вокруг яркой звезды Сириус в нижней части фотографии. Египетское название Сириуса (и прилегающих областей) — Сопдет (греч.: Сотис). Гелиакический восход Сириуса летом был предвестником египетского нового года. 

Двигаясь на север, мы можем заметить голубоватую звезду. Это Альхена, одна из звезд в ногах зодиакального созвездия Близнецов, чьи яркие головные звезды находились бы за верхним левым краем фотографии. В верхнем центре мы можем видеть звезду Эльнат, в созвездии Возничего. Он связан с Эрихтонием, героем греческой мифологии, считающимся изобретателем четырехконной колесницы. Эта же звезда также считается кончиком верхнего рога Тельца, быка. В греческой мифологии Телец связан с богом Зевсом, который послал его похитить принцессу. Общеизвестно, что эта греческая история была придумана, чтобы включить вавилонское созвездие в греческую мифологию. В месопотамской саге о Гильгамеше, которая является одним из старейших известных нам литературных произведений (восходящим к 3-му тысячелетию), Телец — это небесный бык, посланный ревнивой богиней и побежденный царем Урука, чтобы спасти свой народ. На небе он содержит несколько интересных астрономических объектов.

media.caption_en:
The constellation Orion along with its bright stars and surrounding constellations. Orion is surrounded by (going clockwise from the top) Taurus, Eridanus, Lepus, Monoceros and Gemini. Orion’s brightest stars Betelgeuse and Rigel appear at the northern (upper on this diagram) and southern (lower) end of the constellation respectively with the famous three star “belt” in the middle.

Orion spans the celestial equator and is thus visible at some time in the year from all of planet Earth. In the most arctic or antarctic regions of the world, some parts of the constellation may not be visible. Orion is most visible in the evenings in the northern hemisphere winter and southern hemisphere summer. The blue line above Orion marks the ecliptic, the path the Sun appears to travel across the sky over the course of a year. The Sun never passes through Orion, but one can occasionally find the other planets of the Solar System and the Moon in Orion.

Just south of Orion’s belt lie two Messier objects M42 (the Orion nebula) and M43, marked by green squares. These nebulae along with M78 (here the green square to the left of the belt) are part of the huge Orion Molecular Cloud Complex. This covers most of the constellation and includes regions where these molecular clouds are collapsing to form young starts. 

The y-axis of this diagram is in degrees of declination with north as up and the x-axis is in hours of right ascension with east to the left. The sizes of the stars marked here relate to the star's apparent magnitude, a measure of its apparent brightness. The larger dots represent brighter stars. The Greek letters mark the brightest stars in the constellation. These are ranked by brightness with the brightest star being labeled alpha, the second brightest beta, etc., although this ordering is not always followed exactly. The circle around Betelgeuse indicates that it is a variable star. The dotted boundary lines mark the IAU's boundaries of the constellations and the solid green lines mark one of the common forms used to represent the figures of the constellations. Neither the constellation boundaries, nor the line marking the ecliptic, nor the lines joining the stars appear on the sky.

Созвездие Орион вместе с его яркими звёздами и окружающими созвездиями. Орион окружён (по часовой стрелке сверху) Тельцом, Эриданом, Зайцем, Единорогом и Близнецами. Ярчайшие звёзды Ориона Бетельгейзе и Ригель видны соответственно на северном (верхнем на этой диаграмме) и южном (нижнем) конце созвездия, а знаменитый «пояс» из трёх звёзд находится в середине.

Орион пересекает небесный экватор и поэтому виден в какое-то время года со всей планеты Земля. В самых арктических или антарктических регионах мира некоторые части созвездия могут быть не видны. Орион лучше всего виден по вечерам зимой в Северном полушарии и летом в Южном полушарии. Синяя линия над Орионом обозначает эклиптику — путь, который Солнце, как кажется, проходит по небу в течение года. Солнце никогда не проходит через Орион, но иногда в Орионе можно найти другие планеты Солнечной системы и Луну.

Чуть южнее пояса Ориона находятся два объекта Мессье M42 (туманность Ориона) и M43, отмеченные зелёными квадратами. Эти туманности вместе с M78 (здесь зелёный квадрат слева от пояса) являются частью огромного молекулярного облачного комплекса Ориона. Он охватывает большую часть созвездия и включает области, где эти молекулярные облака коллапсируют, образуя молодые звёзды.

Размеры отмеченных здесь звёзд связаны с видимой звёздной величиной звезды — мерой её видимой яркости. Более крупные точки представляют более яркие звёзды. Греческие буквы обозначают самые яркие звёзды в созвездии. Они ранжированы по яркости: самая яркая звезда обозначается альфой, вторая по яркости — бетой и т. д., хотя этот порядок не всегда соблюдается точно. Круг вокруг Бетельгейзе указывает на то, что это переменная звезда. Пунктирные границы обозначают границы созвездий, установленные МАС, а сплошные зелёные линии обозначают одну из распространённых форм, используемых для изображения фигур созвездий. The zodiac constellation Gemini and its surrounding constellations. Starting from the top of the diagram and going clockwise, these are Auriga, Taurus, Lynx, Orion, Monoceros, Canis Minor and Cancer. The brightest stars in Gemini, Castor and Pollux appear in the upper lefthand corner (north-east) of the diagram. In Greek mythology, the stars in this constellation are thought to resemble twins with their arms wrapped around each other, with Castor and Pollux indicating their heads. Gemini lies on the ecliptic (shown here as a blue line), this is the path the Sun appears to take across the sky over the course of a year. The Sun is in Gemini from late June to late July. Just to the right of the foot of the Castor twin is an open cluster of stars (labelled as a yellow circle with a dotted line border), Messier 35, also known as the Shoe-Buckle Cluster. This cluster is spread out over an area roughly the size of the full moon. In addition to this cluster of stars, there is a planetary nebula (labelled as a green circle with four radial spikes) – NGC 2392 – near the celestial equator and just to the left of the Pollux twin. Two variable stars (Mekbuda and Propus; labelled as two concentric circles) can be found in the “legs” of each twin, but are so faint that an observer would need dark skies to see them.

Зодиакальное созвездие Близнецов и окружающие его созвездия. Начиная с верхней части диаграммы и двигаясь по часовой стрелке, это Возничий, Телец, Рысь, Орион, Единорог, Малый Пёс и Рак. Самые яркие звёзды в Близнецах, Кастор и Поллукс, находятся в верхнем левом углу (северо-восток) диаграммы. В греческой мифологии звёзды этого созвездия считаются похожими на близнецов, обнимающих друг друга, причём Кастор и Поллукс обозначают их головы. Близнецы лежат на эклиптике (показана здесь синей линией) — это путь, который Солнце, как кажется, проходит по небу в течение года. Солнце находится в Близнецах с конца июня до конца июля. Другие планеты Солнечной системы также часто можно найти в Близнецах.

Близнецы находятся к северу от небесного экватора и видны во всех регионах мира, кроме антарктических. Близнецы лучше всего видны по вечерам зимой в Северном полушарии и летом в Южном полушарии.

Две переменные звезды (Мекбуда и Пропус; обозначены двумя концентрическими окружностями) можно найти в «ногах» каждого близнеца, но они настолько слабы, что наблюдателю потребуется тёмное небо, чтобы их увидеть.

Греческие буквы обозначают самые яркие звёзды в созвездии. Они ранжированы по яркости: самая яркая звезда обозначается альфой, вторая по яркости — бетой и т. д., хотя этот порядок не всегда соблюдается точно. media.caption_en:
The constellation Auriga with its bright stars and surrounding constellations. Auriga is surrounded by (going clockwise from the top): Camelopardalis, Perseus, Taurus, Gemini and Lynx. Capella, the brightest star in Auriga, is the sixth brightest star in the night sky.

As a northern constellation, Auriga is visible from the whole of the northern hemisphere at some point in the year. The whole of the constellation is visible to equatorial regions of the southern hemisphere with parts of it visible to temperate southern regions. The whole constellation is circumpolar from arctic regions. The constellation is best viewed in the evening in the late northern hemisphere winter and late southern hemisphere summer. 

Auriga lies in the plane of the Milky Way and thus hosts a number of open clusters. Of these M36, M37 and M38 are marked on this diagram with yellow circles. IC 405, also known as the flaming star nebula, is marked here with a green square.

The y-axis of this diagram is in degrees of declination with north as up and the x-axis is in hours of right ascension with east to the left. The sizes of the stars marked here relate to the star's apparent magnitude, a measure of its apparent brightness. The larger dots represent brighter stars. The Greek letters mark the brightest stars in the constellation. These are ranked by brightness with the brightest star being labeled alpha, the second brightest beta, etc., although this ordering is not always followed exactly. The dotted boundary lines mark the IAU's boundaries of the constellations and the solid green lines mark one of the common forms used to represent the figures of the constellations. The blue line at the bottom of the diagram marks the ecliptic. Neither the constellation boundaries, nor the line marking the ecliptic, nor the lines joining the stars appear on the sky.
media.caption_ru:
Созвездие Возничий с его яркими звёздами и окружающими созвездиями. Возничий окружён (по часовой стрелке сверху): Жирафом, Персеем, Тельцом, Близнецами и Рысью. Капелла, самая яркая звезда в Возничем, является шестой по яркости звездой ночного неба.

Будучи северным созвездием, Возничий виден со всего северного полушария в какое-то время года. Всё созвездие видно из экваториальных районов южного полушария, а его части видны из умеренных южных районов. Всё созвездие является незаходящим в арктических районах. Лучше всего созвездие видно по вечерам в конце зимы в северном полушарии и в конце лета в южном полушарии.

Возничий лежит в плоскости Млечного Пути и поэтому содержит ряд рассеянных скоплений. Из них M36, M37 и M38 отмечены на этой диаграмме жёлтыми кружками. IC 405, также известная как туманность Пылающая звезда, отмечена здесь зелёным квадратом.

Ось y этой диаграммы выражена в градусах склонения, север вверху, а ось x — в часах прямого восхождения, восток слева. Размеры отмеченных здесь звёзд связаны с видимой звёздной величиной звезды — мерой её видимой яркости. Более крупные точки представляют более яркие звёзды. Греческие буквы обозначают самые яркие звёзды в созвездии. Они ранжированы по яркости: самая яркая звезда обозначается альфой, вторая по яркости — бетой и т. д., хотя этот порядок не всегда соблюдается точно. Пунктирные границы обозначают границы созвездий, установленные МАС, а сплошные зелёные линии обозначают одну из распространённых форм, используемых для изображения фигур созвездий. Синяя линия внизу диаграммы обозначает эклиптику. Ни границы созвездий, ни линия, обозначающая эклиптику, ни линии, соединяющие звёзды, не видны на небе.
